pages.text: NTM built it to measure how bad things are. Around here it measures how good they're about to get.

pages.title: The Dowsing Rod
pages.text: Hold the geiger counter in either hand and it moonlights as an ore-dowsing rod. Once a second it sweeps six blocks in every direction from your boots for buried $(l:orespawn_integrations:ores_gems/ruby)Ruby$(), $(l:orespawn_integrations:ores_gems/titanium)Titanium$() and $(l:orespawn_integrations:ores_gems/uranium)Uranium$(), then sings about the strongest thing it found. Works in every dimension the veins do — the $(l:orespawn_integrations:dimensions/mining_dimension)Mining Dimension$()'s crowded seams read exactly the same.

pages.title: Know Your Bands
pages.text: Three ores, three songs. Learn them and the ground reads like sheet music.

pages.title: The 2 / 8 / 22 Scale
pages.text: The counter feeds signal strength straight into HBM's own audio bands. Ruby reads $(thing)2$() — a lazy, curious click. Titanium reads $(thing)8$() — steady chatter. An OreSpawn uranium vein reads $(thing)22$() — the full panic song.$(p)Storage blocks count too: a wall of uranium blocks sings exactly like the vein it came from, which turns vault-hunting into a listening exercise.

pages.title: Zero. Always Zero.
pages.text: Your dose stays at exactly zero the whole time — right-click the counter and watch it swear to that in writing. We drive HBM's telemetry channel, never its radiation: detection and harm are separate wires, and we only touch the one that can't bite.$(p)The first vein you ping signs the $(thing)First Ping$() advancement. NTM's dosimeter overhears the same signal, if you prefer your prospecting on a wristwatch.
